name: Varun Beverages Ltd
title: Varun Beverages Ltd - 540180 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volume up 19.8% and India up 14.4% in H1-quarter, but management gave no capacity-discipline signal; margin cushioned by early raw-material stocking and a Twizza mix drag of 76 bps.

triggers.label: India volume growth 14.4% in Q2
triggers.quote: resulting in overall volume growth for the quarter of 14.4%

triggers.label: PepsiCo licence extended to 2049
triggers.quote: extended our exclusive bottling and trademark license agreement with PepsiCo in India until April 2049

triggers.label: Realisation per case up 1.2%
triggers.quote: Net realization per case for beverages at the consolidated level improved by 1.2%

triggers.label: Net debt ~Rs 3,730 mn post Twizza
triggers.quote: At the consolidated level, net debt stood at ~Rs. 3,730 million as of 30th June 2026

summary.headline: VBL Q2 CY2026 revenue rose 20.4% to Rs 84,512.3 mn and EBITDA 17.2% to Rs 23,430.4 mn, with India volume up 14.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales volume grew 19.8% to 466.7 million cases in the quarter, with net revenue up 20.4% year-on-year. India volume grew 14.4%, with growth of about 20% or more in every month since March except April, which was roughly flat due to El Nino-driven rain. International volumes rose 38.4%, including 11.8 million cases from the newly consolidated Twizza business in South Africa. EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, while India margin improved 38 bps. Management also extended the PepsiCo bottling licence to April 2049 and announced the Calpis tie-up with Asahi and the Devyani Kenya acquisition.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (net of excise and GST)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value), cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 14.4% in Q2 with 20%+ monthly growth from March except April (about flat). India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps on operating efficiencies, partly offset by higher transport and distribution costs. Low-sugar/no-sugar products were about 73% of consolidated volume in H1.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume rose 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa; ex-Twizza growth was above 25%. Management said all African markets are growing except Zambia, which is small and slower. Twizza operates at lower margins, which diluted group EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Value-added dairy (VAD) and Nimbooz
segments.commentary: Management said VAD is growing above 40% and Nimbooz above 30% for the company, about 3x-4x the overall business. Growth figures were given only as ranges, with no absolute values.

segments.name: Food distribution and manufacturing in Africa
segments.commentary: Management said this business is growing about 50%. No absolute figures or targets were given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India growth of at least 20% month-on-month after June, with July tracking the same trend.
Management said India can keep growing in double digits despite a stronger competitive field from Campa and Coca-Cola, and argued the industry is growing about 20%.

Raw material costs have risen with the West Asia crisis. Part of the increase is booked in Q2 under average costing, and the balance will hit Q3. Management said the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.
Management said EBITDA margins can be maintained even in a high-crude year and would improve once the conflicts ease.
Energy drink labels must drop the word 'energy' within 90 days, per the regulator's guidance. Management said volumes are returning to STING as new labels roll out.
Management will not scale Rs 10 pricing for now, as it is not profitable for the company, unless monthly growth falls below 20%.
capex_capacity: H1 net capitalised capex of ~Rs 9,500 mn: ~Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India including a value-added dairy line at Supa, ~Rs 1,000 mn for a snack plant in Zimbabwe, and ~Rs 4,000 mn for market infrastructure (visi-coolers, glass bottles, pallets, vehicles).
Capital work-in-progress of ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026, mainly South Africa expansion and a CSD line in Kenya.
Inorganic capex of Rs 11,314 mn for the Twizza Limited acquisition in South Africa.
Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) business acquisition agreed, giving a ready go-to-market for CSDs and energy drinks in Kenya.
Twizza in South Africa helped overcome capacity constraints, with the company strengthening its manufacturing and route-to-market footprint there.
demand_pricing: India Q2 volume +14.4%, with April about flat due to heavy rain. May seasonality has shifted (it used to be about 15% of business before 2025), and management says non-weather months show high double-digit growth.
Rs 10 price point: management said it has not scaled it up because it is not profitable and the company is growing 20%+ without it. Some markets are pushing Rs 10 packs, but the mix is small.
Pack changes: the company is upsizing and downsizing packs by market. Management said volume is reported on an 8-ounce basis, and realisation per 8-ounce case and gross margin are said to be stable.
Competition: Campa Cola is expanding at Rs 10 and Rs 20 price points, and management said the Rs 20 gap has narrowed. The 400 ml Rs 20 pack is driving recruitment.
GST cuts: management said the impact on dairy, water and soda was minimal. Some prices were held despite geopolitical cost pressure.
Management declined to give market share data, saying it does not track share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to scale the Rs 10 price point, and how much of the April weakness was rain versus competition from Campa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not scaling Rs 10 because it is unprofitable. It said India is growing 20%+ month-on-month outside April, which was hit by El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into alcobev in India, and is it bidding for Bira?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only looking at possible new categories and is not bidding for Bira. Prathmesh Mishra was hired for the group, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: Can India grow at low double digits given stronger competitors and a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ravi Jaipuria said H1 India growth was 14.4% and July is continuing at the same trend, so double-digit growth looks achievable. Varun Jaipuria said weather, not demand, was holding back growth in months without rain.

qa_highlights.question: Up to what crude level can margins be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are maintainable even in a worse geopolitical year and that margins cannot get worse once conflicts ease. It did not give a crude threshold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the energy drink labelling change on STING?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June and July saw a temporary dip as volume moved to CSD. Volumes are returning as new labels roll out, and the regulator gave 90 days to remove the word 'energy'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Calpis tie-up extend to other Asahi brands or other categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current focus is stabilising Calpis. Dairy is a core category, and no decision has been made on RTD tea or coffee.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from the West Asia crisis: part of the cost is in Q2 under average costing, and the balance hits Q3.
Monsoon and El Nino weather volatility, which hurt April and shifted the seasonal pattern of May.
Lower Twizza margins, which pulled group EBITDA margin down 76 bps; further integration and dilution is possible.
Energy drink labelling change, with a 90-day compliance deadline. Some volume shifted to CSD in June-July.
Rising competitive intensity from Campa Cola's Rs 10 and Rs 20 packs and Coca-Cola, which could pressure India volume and pricing.
Net debt of ~Rs 3,730 mn at consolidated level after the Twizza acquisition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and margins, with management repeatedly citing 20%+ growth and calling the margin outlook comfortable. It was evasive on Rs 10 scale-up, market share, Bira and PepsiCo's share data, and deferred on the Calpis expansion and new categories.
key_quotes: If you see our growth, which is March onwards, we are growing healthily at 20% plus.
We can comfortably maintain our margins even in a year, which is the worst year for the geopolitical reasons and all the costing has gone up internationally.
Cans is 1- 2% of our business, nothing major.
Largely our portfolio is low sugar or Zero Sugar as you call it.

adds.what: Value-added dairy line at Supa (India), part of ~Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India capex
Snack plant in Zimbabwe (~Rs 1,000 mn capex)
South Africa expansion and Kenya CSD line (capital WIP ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026); no capacity numbers or timing given

growth.why: Management guides India growth of at least 20% month-on-month after June and double-digit growth despite stronger competition, backed by 20%+ monthly run-rate since March and the Devyani Kenya acquisition, but no specific new plant capacity or order numbers were given beyond modest capex lines.
